The Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, has threatened to commit the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), to prison over the continued detention of five Okuama community leaders and indigenes despite an order for their immediate release. The court issued a Form 48 notice, warning Fagbemi that failure to comply with its release order would amount to contempt of court and could attract imprisonment. The notice, dated November 11, 2026, was titled, “Notice of Consequences of Disobedience to Order of Court” and addressed to the Attorney-General of the Federation at the Federal Ministry of Justice, Abuja. It specifically demanded the immediate release of Prof. Arthur Ekpekpo, Mr James Oghoroko, Chief Belvis Adogbo, Mr Dennis Okugbaye and Ms Mabel Owhemu, who are applicants in Suit No. FHC/WR/CS/42/2024. The warning states, “Take notice that unless you obey the injunction contained in the court order overleaf for the immediate release of the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th and 6th applicants from detention, you will be guilty of contempt of court and will be liable to be committed to prison.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The suit was filed by the applicants for themselves and on behalf of the people of Okuama community in Ewu Kingdom, Ughelli South Local Government Area of Delta State. The case lists the Federal Government, the Attorney-General of the Federation, the Armed Forces of the Federation, the Minister of Defence and the Chief of Defence Staff as respondents. The Form 48 followed a June 10, 2026 court order, which, according to information provided in connection with the case, directed the release of the five applicants from detention. The development is the latest in the legal battle over the detention of Okuama community members following the killing of 17 military personnel in the community on March 14, 2024. The incident triggered a military operation in Okuama, during which the community was destroyed, and several residents were arrested. Among those arrested on August 18, 2024, were Ekpekpo, a lecturer at Delta State University, Abraka, and President-General of Ewu Kingdom, alongside other community leaders. Following their continued detention without trial, the affected persons approached the Federal High Court in Warri to challenge their detention. The latest notice places the Attorney-General on formal notice of the consequences of failing to comply with the court’s directive. Although the Form 48 warns that Fagbemi could be committed to prison, it does not mean that he has been convicted of contempt or sentenced to imprisonment. The form is a formal warning that further contempt proceedings could follow if the court’s order is disobeyed. Efecha Gold
